t: An open four-legged research robot with twelve force-controlled joints.
steps: Read the Solo12 build guide in the Open Dynamic Robot Initiative hardware repo on GitHub.
Check the parts list and budget for the motion sensor, tools, and tax on top of the estimate.
Order the circuit boards from the open Gerber files and print the plastic parts.
Build and test one actuator module with its motor, encoder, and belts.
Flash the master board firmware with the free ESP-IDF tools and the driver boards with TI tools.
Set up a real-time Linux PC and install the odri_control_interface software.
Run the robot model in the PyBullet simulator before you power the real legs.
Ask questions on the ODRI forum as you assemble and calibrate the joints.
